# Independent audit: sharp dimensional weighted three centroid tails


`candidate bb74919333cc624f`, checked its
one-constraint localization against the primary theorem, reconstructed
the scalar branch analysis, checked the displayed exact polynomial
certificates, and reran both the new verifier and the archived quadrature
verifier. No mathematical repair is needed.

The audited conclusion is the ordinary convex-body inequality

    F(0)+F(s)+lambda_d F(-s) >= Gamma_d+lambda_d

for every real shift, with the stated optimal coefficient, and its sharp
measurable-subset consequence. It is not an unrestricted mixed-integer
depth theorem and does not authorize reusing the central term in several
pair payments.

## 1. Localization and all boundary conventions

I checked Theorems 1 and 2 and the density-parameter conversion in the
[author-uploaded primary paper of Fradelizi and Guedon](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220452814_The_Extreme_Points_of_Subsets_of_s_-Concave_Probabilities_and_a_Geometric_Localization_Theorem).
The needed reduction is precisely its one-integral-constraint theorem;
no localization with two independent equalities is being assumed.

The source marginal is nonatomic and its probability-concavity parameter
is 1/d, whereas its density exponent is 1/(d-1). For d>=2 the measure
parameter is within the theorem's permitted range. A compact interval
containing the original support is fixed before applying the theorem.
The condition integral x dnu>=0 uses a continuous constraint function.

For a strict violation, moving only the central CDF threshold from zero
to -epsilon preserves the violation by continuity. All three threshold
sets are closed in the fixed interval, and all their coefficients are
positive, so their weighted sum is an affine upper-semicontinuous
functional on probabilities. An admissible Dirac has location x>=0 and
can contribute only to the positive threshold. Its value is at most one,
strictly below 2-Gamma_d. This includes a Dirac at zero, which would be
problematic without the epsilon regularization.

Every non-Dirac alternative has mean exactly zero and affine-power
density with exponent d-1 on an interval. Its regularized objective is
bounded above by the unregularized objective proved in the scalar
argument. The extra one-sided moment condition in the primary theorem
causes no additional case: a nondegenerate centered interval law has
strictly positive proper final first moments. The proof therefore never
passes an unshifted central CDF through an atomic limit.

Actual full-dimensional bodies and the non-Dirac affine-power laws give
zero mass to scalar support endpoints and to every ambient cutting
hyperplane. Thus all displayed closed-cap/CDF conversions remain exact
at supporting cuts. Constant densities and d=1 are treated separately;
the latter has paired tails summing to one for every real shift.

## 2. Constants, scalar normalization, and powered-mean concavity

Writing a0=d/(d+1), p=d-1, and k=lambda_d^(1/p), I verified

    (1+k)^p = 2^d Gamma_d.

The arithmetic-geometric-mean comparison with L=4 Gamma_d^2 yields
lambda_d<=L<1. Combining this with 4 Gamma_d(1-Gamma_d)<=1 gives
lambda_d<=Gamma_d/(1-Gamma_d), exactly the condition required at zero
shift. For negative shifts, subtracting the positive-shift expression
gives (1-lambda_d)[F(s)-F(-s)]>=0 when s<0. The reduction to positive
shifts has the correct sign.

Every nonconstant nonnegative affine-power law has one of the two
orientations of the normalized density d x^(d-1)/(1-r^d), r<=x<=1.
The mean formula, the inequality m>=(1+r)/2, and c=2m-1>=r are correct.

I independently differentiated g(R)=I(R)^(1/alpha), alpha=1/d. Its
second derivative is exactly

    (1-alpha) I^(1/alpha-2) (A^2-I B).

Cauchy-Schwarz proves the sign on 0<R<1; continuity extends concavity
to R=0,1 without assuming bounded second derivatives there. The chord
from g(0)=Gamma_d to g(1)=1 gives p0>=Gamma_d. Jensen gives
g(R)<=(1+R)/2 and hence p0<=1/2. The mean is strictly increasing, as
follows directly from its integral representation.

## 3. Reflected orientation and sharp critical branch

On 0<=s<=1-m both CDF arguments remain in support. The derivative of
J(s)=G(m-s)+lambda_d G(m+s) changes from negative to positive at
s_*=m(1-k)/(1+k), if this point occurs before the upper endpoint.
After s=1-m the first CDF decreases and the other equals one, so J
decreases to lambda_d. Thus the stated stationary and constant branches
exhaust every possible global minimum, including supporting cuts and
large shifts.

Substitution at the stationary point gives

    p0+J(s_*) = [(1+lambda_d/Gamma_d)g(R)
                  -(2+lambda_d)R]/(1-R).

After subtracting the proposed lower bound, the numerator is exactly the
function H in the source. It is concave. The critical branch exists on
the interval 0<=R<=R_*: its upper mean threshold (1+k)/2 lies strictly
between a0 and one. At R=0, H=0. At R_*, the upper threshold is one,
and the original expression is p0+G(2m-1)+lambda_d, which is at least
Gamma_d+lambda_d. These two endpoint checks give H>=0 throughout the
entire feasible stationary interval. No unsupported claim that an
untruncated cone minimizes every frustum expression is used.

## 4. Increasing orientation and the finite exact certificates

The derivative is -f(m+s)+lambda_d f(m-s) until s=1-m and is
nonnegative afterwards. The global minimum is consequently
1-p0+lambda_d(1-T). This gives exactly the scalar inequality
p0+lambda_d T<=1-Gamma_d.

With the source's polynomials U,W, the identity

    P_d,l / [(1-r^d) W^d] = 1-Gamma_d-p0-lT

is exact. All denominators are positive on 0<=r<1. The division by
1-r, the degree d^2-1, and the power-to-Bernstein conversion are correct.
For d=2, the numerator derivative of the displayed cubic is
147(r-1/7)^2+3, and the cubic starts at two.

I checked all complete coefficient lists through the independent
rational reconstruction in the verifier. The d=3,4,5 Bernstein vectors
match exactly; the d=6 monomial vector matches exactly and is entirely
positive. The reported minimum Bernstein coefficients 2,32,502,8712
also check. This is a finite algebraic certificate on the whole closed
parameter interval, not a numerical grid argument. The d=3,...,6 use
of l=1 is stronger than needed because 0<lambda_d<=1 and T>=0.

## 5. The all-dimensional quadrature dependency

I reread the proof in Section 5 of
`candidate 732b11a769399016`, rather than
assuming the bound T<=1/6 from its statement. Its logarithmic difference
has derivative

    (v-1)(5v-1)(5v-2) / [2v(1+5v)^2].

The only possible minima on (0,1] are v=1 and v=1/5. At the latter,
the four displayed positive atanh-series terms prove log(5)>8/5
exactly. The substitution v=(R+t)/(1+t) gives the stated reciprocal
integral inequality with the correct direction. Multiplying by the
positive Stieltjes kernel converts it into the power quadrature bound.
All individual integrals are finite for 0<alpha<1, including at R=0;
there is no subtraction of divergent terms.

At alpha=1/d the mean representation is exact. Since 2m-1>=r>=0,
raising the quadrature inequality to the d-th power preserves its sign
and gives T<=1/6. This dependency is proved for every integer d>=2;
the new note uses it only for d>=7.

The monotonicity of Gamma_d, the bound lambda_d<=4 Gamma_d^2,
and p0<=1/2 reduce those dimensions to the exact positive gap

    1/2-Gamma_7-(2/3)Gamma_7^2
      =29669536175/6597069766656.

The arithmetic is correct. Constant affine densities have minimum
1/2+lambda_d, so they are not omitted by either orientation argument.

## 6. Optimality and actual measurable subsets

For the reflected cone law, v=(2a0)^(-1/(d-1)) satisfies
v^d=1/(1+k) and 2a0-v=kv. The shift v-a0 is positive because
2 Gamma_d<1, and both cuts are proper. The ratio of the positive-shift
tail to the deficit of the negative-shift tail is exactly lambda_d.
Thus this actual simplex marginal gives equality and rules out every
larger coefficient. The interval gives the d=1 sharpness separately.
The expansion yielding lambda_d -> 4/e^2 is correct. The optional
lambda_d>1/2 statement has the stated elementary dependency in the
previous weighted-tail note and is not needed for the new proof.

For arbitrary measurable E subset K, the capacity inequality
|E intersect H_t|>=max(0,a-V+F(t)) is valid without convexity. After
subtracting lambda_d a, its minimum over 0<=a<=V occurs at
a=V-F(t): the two slopes are -lambda_d and 1-lambda_d. Applying the
weighted theorem at shift -t gives the claimed payment for every sign
of t, including endpoint values a=0,V. Every subset of a null cutting
hyperplane remains null, so no regularity of the boundary of E is needed.

The sharpness choice E=K intersect {u.(x-g)<=-s_*} has positive volume,
zero E-cap volume at its supporting threshold, and exactly the claimed
remaining payment. This is a convex cap subbody. At three consecutive
integer bases, the fibers E,K,K are indeed the exact fibers of their
convex hull because (E+K)/2 is contained in K. An arbitrary measurable
E need not have such a convex realization; the source correctly makes
that geometric statement only when E is convex.

## 7. Verification and dependency boundary

Commands rerun successfully with standard Python:

    python3 supporting computation verify_sharp_dimensional_weighted_three_tails.py
    python3 supporting computation verify_paired_centroid_tail_scalar_certificates.py

The first reconstructs every displayed coefficient vector, checks 505
exact frustum identities, and checks the dimension-seven constant and
the planar equality/subset calibration. The second verifies the exact
quadrature derivative and logarithmic certificate. The symbolic scalar
proof and primary localization theorem, rather than these finite sample
checks, supply the all-parameter and all-dimensional assertions.

Dependency order is: primary one-constraint localization and ordinary
Grunbaum; elementary powered-mean concavity and archived quadrature;
the two scalar orientations; the all-body weighted theorem; then the
measurable-subset payment. There is no dependence on OC or on an
unproved mixed-integer selector, and no circular use of the new weighted
inequality in its own scalar closure.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
